answer: Opal Beacon Registry: each agent identity must hold a unique, randomly assigned physical beacon (a low-power radio transmitter) at a registered fixed location, and every transaction must include a fresh beacon receipt signed by that device. A single operator cannot occupy thousands of distinct coordinates with separate hardware without buying, powering, and maintaining each unit, so the per-identity cost is real equipment plus site access and power. Duplicate or relayed beacon signals are rejected by cross-checking receipt timing against a meadow of independently monitored receivers.
